summary: Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Harvard under George David Birkhoff and held mathematics professorships at Banaras Hindu University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.
Dan Arnold works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago and held faculty appointments at McGill University and the University of Chicago.
Dan Li is a scholar of linguistics and Buddhist studies who studied under Sherab Gyatso. She was attested as an associate professor at Soka University in 2026.

Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, holding a Ph.D. from Temple University. His career includes posts at Florida State University, the University of Georgia, and a research associateship at Harvard University.

Dan Martin is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University Bloomington under Elliot Sperling. He held positions at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and Carnegie Mellon University.

Dan Smyer Yü is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD from the University of California, Davis. He served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who completed his PhD under Rudolf Bernet at KU Leuven and his Habilitation at the University of Copenhagen. He has served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen and the University of Oxford.

Daniel Aaron Getz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He was attested as an associate professor at Bradley University in 2019.
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Daniel B. Stevenson is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his Ph.D. at Columbia University. He held assistant professorships at Butler University and the University of Kansas, and served as a Guest Scholar at Soka University.
Daniel Baum is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his BA at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and his doctorate at Leiden University under the supervision of Alexander Lubotsky.
Daniel Borengasser works in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.
Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair and became an associate professor at Cornell University.
Daniel Clarke Waugh is a historian of Iranian and Central Asian studies who was educated at Yale and Harvard. He was appointed to a post at the University of Washington in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as president of the University of California, founding president of Johns Hopkins University, and president of both the Carnegie Institution and the American Oriental Society.

Daniel Cozort specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and taught at Bates College and Dickinson College.

Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He served as a director of research at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique and at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III.

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Harvard University, where he studied under Walter Eugene Clark and Willard Van Orman Quine. He was appointed professor at Harvard University in 1939.

Daniel John Gogerly was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He headed the Wesleyan Mission Press, chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society, and served as secretary, vice-president, and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka.

Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who completed his doctorate at the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a professor at the University of British Columbia from around 1973 to 2001.
